claim: For all integer partitions lam, mu, nu with |lam| = |mu| + |nu| and c^{lam}_{mu nu} > 0, every coefficient of the stretched Littlewood-Richardson polynomial P(t) = c^{t lam}_{t mu, t nu} in the monomial basis 1, t, t^2, ... is nonnegative (the King-Tollu-Toumazet positivity conjecture, 2004), and the attack seeks a proof.

quadruple.statement: For all integer partitions lam, mu, nu with |lam| = |mu| + |nu| and c^{lam}_{mu nu} > 0, every coefficient of the stretched Littlewood-Richardson polynomial P(t) = c^{t lam}_{t mu, t nu} in the monomial basis 1, t, t^2, ... is nonnegative (the King-Tollu-Toumazet positivity conjecture, 2004), and the attack seeks a proof.
quadruple.stage: Ehrhart theory of the Knutson-Tao hive polytopes H(lam, mu, nu) in R^D, D <= (n-1)(n-2)/2 for n parts, cut out by rhombus inequalities whose normals lie in the finite set N_n of 0/+-1 vectors, together with the two structures a proof must use: McMullen local formulas (a_k = sum over k-faces F of alpha(normal cone of F) times the relative volume of F, with alpha depending only on the normal cone and not unique, Ring-Schuermann 2017), and Rassart's chamber-wise polynomiality (for fixed n each a_k is a polynomial homogeneous of degree k on each chamber of the Littlewood-Richardson chamber complex, so a_1 is piecewise linear)

shape.objects: Triples (lam, mu, nu) of integer partitions with |lam| = |mu| + |nu| and c > 0: an infinite set graded by the number of parts n and the size |lam|. For each triple: the integer-valued polynomial P of degree dim H and the rational polytope H (vertex denominators 1 for n <= 4, up to 7 observed at n = 7). For a proof the objects are two levels up: the finitely many combinatorial types of normal cones of faces of hive polytopes of a fixed side n, and the local formulas (weight functions alpha on rational cones satisfying McMullen's balancing conditions), of which the Berline-Vergne valuation is one member of an affine family.
shape.quantifiers: Universal over the infinite set of triples and over the coefficient index: for all (lam, mu, nu), for all k, a_k >= 0. For each fixed n the statement is finite in principle: by Rassart the function (lam, mu, nu) -> a_k is a polynomial Q_{Delta,k} homogeneous of degree k on each closed chamber Delta of the Littlewood-Richardson chamber complex of rank n, so the statement for rank n is 'each of finitely many polynomials is nonnegative on its closed rational cone', decidable over the reals; and for k = 1 each Q_{Delta,1} is linear, so nonnegativity on Delta holds if and only if it holds at the finitely many extreme rays of Delta.
shape.target_quantity: A decision: true (a proof for every triple) or false (one exhibited triple with a certified negative coefficient). No constant is asked for; a natural strengthening does carry one, the largest c with a_k >= c times the corresponding coefficient of the unimodular simplex for every hive polytope, whose value over the verified box is 24/25.
shape.ambient_structure: Four kinds of structure coexist: (i) representation theory and symmetric functions (c is the multiplicity of s_lam in s_mu s_nu, counted by Littlewood-Richardson tableaux); (ii) polyhedral geometry (c is the number of lattice points of H, P its Ehrhart polynomial, H(t lam, t mu, t nu) = t H); (iii) the Horn / Littlewood-Richardson cone with its essential Horn facets and its chamber complex (Rassart 2004), on which the coefficients are piecewise polynomial; (iv) valuation theory: McMullen's local formulas write each Ehrhart coefficient as a sum of face volumes weighted by a function of the normal cone alone, the weights are far from unique (Ring-Schuermann, arXiv:1709.10390), and the Berline-Vergne valuation is the standard choice.
shape.symmetries: c^{lam}_{mu nu} = c^{lam}_{nu mu}; column addition c^{lam + (1^n)}_{mu + (1^n), nu} = c^{lam}_{mu nu} for n >= the largest length, which keeps P; complementation in a rectangle (the S_3 symmetry of the triple multiplicity), which keeps P and changes the shape; conjugation keeps c but not P. The rhombus-normal set N_n and hence the family of normal cones is invariant under the dihedral symmetry of the hive triangle, so the finite set of cone types a proof must handle is a union of orbits.
shape.configuration: The forbidden configuration is a sign: a_k < 0 for some k. On the proof side the required configuration is an object: a local formula alpha, nonnegative on every normal cone that occurs at a face of a hive polytope, satisfying McMullen's balancing conditions, so that a_k = sum over k-faces of alpha times relative volume is a sum of nonnegative terms. Algebraic relations that hold unconditionally: a_0 = 1, D! a_D = normalized volume > 0, a_{D-1} = half the normalized boundary volume > 0; for a full-dimensional hive the coefficients of t^D, t^{D-1}, t^{D-2}, t^{D-3} are positive, and for a full-dimensional 5-part hive every coefficient but a_1 is positive (Ferudun 2026). Horn factorisation makes the load-bearing case the primitive (2-connected interior) triples.
shape.extremal_candidate: The polytopes where the coefficients come closest to zero, from the census of the box (6,855,302 polynomials, two implementations): exactly 7,469 have a coefficient below the unimodular-simplex value, and every one of them has exactly D + 1 lattice points (h*_1 = 0), normalized volume 2 and h*-vector (1, 0, 1, 0, ...), in dimensions 4, 5, 6 with minimal ratios 24/25, 44/45, 799/812; at 8 parts one hive polytope with D + 1 lattice points and normalized volume 3 occurs (lam = (4,4,3,3,2,2,1,1), mu = (3,3,2,2,1,1), nu = (3,2,2,1), c = 7, dimension 6, h* = (1, 0, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0), ratio 393/406). The Reeve simplex is the general-polytope object of this shape whose a_1 does go negative (h* = (1, 0, v-1, 0), a_1 = 2 - (v-1)/6), so the extremal question is whether a hive polytope with h*_1 = 0 can have large normalized volume.
shape.finite_certificates: The false side has a finite certificate: one triple with its polynomial and an index k with a_k < 0, re-checkable by an independent counter. The true side has a finite certificate for each fixed n and no known finite certificate uniform in n: for fixed n the finitely many normal-cone types of hive faces make the existence of a nonnegative local formula a linear-programming feasibility question (Farkas dual of Ferudun's (HTE)), and the chamber-wise polynomials make nonnegativity a finite list of polynomial-positivity problems over rational cones, which for k = 1 reduce to finitely many evaluations at the extreme rays of the chambers.
shape.monotonicity: The claim is not monotone in a parameter, but the proof record is a ladder in two parameters. In the number of parts: proved for n <= 4 at every size (Ferudun 2026, Theorem 1); the next rung is n = 5, where only a_1 of full-dimensional hives is open (Ferudun 2026, Theorem 3). In the codimension: the top four coefficients of every full-dimensional hive are proved by termwise positivity of the Berline-Vergne valuation at codimensions 0 to 3, and codimension 4 carries a cone of weight -349/28800, so that route stops there. Verified finite ranges: length <= 7 and size <= 30 (this project, a theorem for length <= 6 and evidence at 7).
shape.uniformity_parameter: The number of parts n. The hive dimension (n-1)(n-2)/2, the number of rhombus normals, the number of normal-cone types of faces, the number of essential Horn triples (12, 41, 142, 521, 2042, 8499 for n = 3..8) and the chamber complex all grow with n, and every known proof is for a fixed small n or a fixed codimension. A proof of the conjecture needs an argument uniform in n; each fixed n is a finite problem.
shape.proof_shape: Four shapes are available. (a) Local formula: choose a McMullen local formula nonnegative on the normal cones of hive faces; termwise Berline-Vergne fails at codimension 4, and by rational Farkas duality the existence of some nonnegative local formula is Ferudun's (HTE), equivalent to <a_q, w> >= 0 for every nonnegative balanced realizable face weight w; for fixed n this is a finite linear program over the cone types that occur. (b) Chamber-wise: for fixed n, prove Q_{Delta,k} >= 0 on each chamber; for k = 1 the polynomial is linear, so it suffices to evaluate at the extreme rays of the chambers. (c) h*-expansion: a_1 = H_D + sum_{i >= 1} (-1)^{i-1} h*_i / (i binom(D, i)), so a_1 >= 0 follows from a bound on the even-index h*-mass, and in particular from a bound on the normalized volume of hive polytopes with h*_1 = 0 (exactly D + 1 lattice points); the observed bound in the record is 2 up to 7 parts and 3 at 8 parts. (d) Reduction: Horn factorisation leaves the primitive triples, and column removal and the symmetries reduce the parameter space. Loss per step: (a) loses nothing but may be infeasible; (b) is exact but grows with the chamber complex; (c) gives only the coefficients whose h*-expansion is controlled.
shape.neighbours: (1) Positivity for length <= 4, all sizes: known true (Ferudun 2026, arXiv:2607.22301). (2) c = 1 implies P = 1 and c = 2 implies P = t + 1: known true. (3) Polynomiality: known true (Derksen-Weyman; Rassart; Thawinrak). (4) Top four coefficients of every full-dimensional hive, and every coefficient but a_1 of a full-dimensional 5-part hive: known true (Ferudun 2026). (5) Ehrhart positivity for marked order polytopes and skew Gelfand-Tsetlin polytopes: known true (Jochemko-Menon, arXiv:2604.08394), but hive polytopes are not marked order polytopes (rhombus inequalities relate four entries) and the Littlewood-Richardson polytope is a fibre of the content map, not a marked order polytope. (6) Ehrhart positivity for matroid polytopes and for generalized permutohedra: known FALSE (Ferroni, arXiv:2105.04465), refuting the conjectures of De Loera-Haws-Koeppe and Castillo-Liu; the same termwise-local-formula heuristic had supported them. (7) Order polytopes: positive up to dimension 13, negative from 14 (Liu-Tsuchiya; Liu-Xin-Zhang). (8) Tesler polytopes: third and fourth coefficients positive (Lee-Liu). (9) The 3 x N transportation image family is Ehrhart positive where computed, and its positivity in general is not in print. (10) Stretched Newell-Littlewood coefficients: positivity conjectured, open (King 2021).
shape.known_bounds: Positive side (proved): length <= 4, all sizes; c <= 2; the top four coefficients of every full-dimensional hive; every coefficient but a_1 of a full-dimensional 5-part hive; the Horn factorisation, which reduces to primitive triples. Verified finite ranges: length <= 6 and size <= 30 by two independent programs, length 7 and size <= 30 by one solver and two encodings (this project's box attack, finished), and 453,799 sampled hives beyond the box with no negative coefficient (this project's negative-side attack, finished). Documented ceilings: termwise Berline-Vergne positivity fails at codimension 4 (a cone of weight -349/28800), so the route that gave the top four coefficients cannot be continued cell by cell; the same class of argument fails outright on matroid polytopes (Ferroni); no proof method in print is uniform in n. Negative side: nothing; no counterexample is known anywhere.
shape.missing_input: One statement: (HTE) of Ferudun 2026, that some McMullen local formula is nonnegative on the normal cones of the faces of hive polytopes, equivalently <a_q, w> >= 0 for every nonnegative balanced realizable face weight w. Two weaker inputs would also close named parts: a bound on the normalized volume of hive polytopes with exactly D + 1 lattice points would give a_1 >= 0 by the h*-expansion, and a nonnegative local formula for the finitely many normal-cone types occurring at n = 5 would give the conjecture for length <= 5 at every size.
shape.base_theory: ZFC. Every instance is a finite integer computation (lattice-point counts of a rational polytope, exact rational interpolation), provable in Peano arithmetic; the proof-side objects are finite too for fixed n (a linear program over finitely many cone types, or polynomial positivity on rational cones, decidable by Tarski elimination); no hypothesis beyond ZFC bears on the claim or on any neighbour. A proof assistant cannot yet state the claim: Mathlib had no Littlewood-Richardson coefficient and no Schur polynomial on 2026-09-03, only YoungDiagram and SemistandardYoungTableau.

known: P(t) = c^{t lam}_{t mu, t nu} is a polynomial in t: Derksen and Weyman, J. Algebra 255 (2002) 247-257, doi:10.1016/S0021-8693(02)00125-4; Rassart, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 107 (2004) 161-179, arXiv:math/0308101 (also the chamber-wise polynomiality of the coefficients in (lam, mu, nu)); Thawinrak, arXiv:2211.06810.

c = the number of integer hives (lattice points of the hive polytope), and saturation: Knutson and Tao, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 12 (1999) 1055-1090, arXiv:math/9807160; the facets of the Littlewood-Richardson cone: Knutson, Tao, Woodward, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 17 (2004) 19-48, arXiv:math/0107011.

The positivity conjecture and the factorisation on saturated Horn facets: King, Tollu, Toumazet, CRM Proc. Lecture Notes 34 (2004) 99-112, doi:10.1090/crmp/034/10; 'The hive model and the polynomial nature of stretched Littlewood-Richardson coefficients', Sem. Lothar. Combin. 54A (2006) B54Ad, https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~slc/wpapers/s54Akitoto1.pdf; J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 116 (2009) 314-333, doi:10.1016/j.jcta.2008.06.005; Cho, Jung, Moon, DMTCS Proc. (2008), doi:10.46298/dmtcs.3592, Theorem 1.3.

c = 1 implies P = 1: Knutson, Tao, Woodward 2004. c = 2 implies P = t + 1: Ikenmeyer, J. Algebraic Combin. 44 (2016) 1-29, arXiv:1209.1521; Sherman, doi:10.1016/j.jalgebra.2017.03.011, arXiv:1505.06551.

Positivity for all triples of length <= 4; the top four coefficients of every full-dimensional hive positive; full-dimensional 5-part hives positive except possibly the linear coefficient; termwise Berline-Vergne positivity fails at codimension 4 (a cell of weight -349/28800); the reduction of the general conjecture to the effectivity statement (HTE), which is <a_q, w> >= 0 for every nonnegative balanced realizable face weight w by rational Farkas duality; the strip construction realising 3 x N transportation polytopes as Littlewood-Richardson polytopes: Ferudun, arXiv:2607.22301 (2026-07-24), with the replay bundle github.com/AlperTheKing/ktt-positivity.

McMullen local formulas: each Ehrhart coefficient is a sum over faces of the relative volume weighted by a function of the normal cone alone, and the weights are far from unique: Ring and Schuermann, arXiv:1709.10390 (also Ring, arXiv:1812.06654). The Berline-Vergne valuation as a tool for Ehrhart positivity: Castillo and Liu, arXiv:1509.07884; Castillo, Liu, Nill, Paffenholz, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 160 (2018) 316-331, arXiv:1704.05532.

The same termwise-local-formula heuristic fails on neighbouring families: matroid polytopes and generalized permutohedra are NOT Ehrhart positive (Ferroni, arXiv:2105.04465, disproving De Loera-Haws-Koeppe and Castillo-Liu); order polytopes are positive up to dimension 13 (Liu, Xin, Zhang, arXiv:2412.07164) and not from dimension 14 (Liu and Tsuchiya, Adv. Appl. Math. 108 (2019), arXiv:1806.08403); smooth lattice polytopes with every possibly-negative coefficient negative exist in every dimension >= 3 (Castillo, Liu, Nill, Paffenholz).

Ehrhart positivity is known for marked order polytopes and skew Gelfand-Tsetlin polytopes: Jochemko and Menon, arXiv:2604.08394 (2026); for Tesler polytopes only the third and fourth coefficients: Lee and Liu, Discrete Comput. Geom. (2022), arXiv:1911.06291, doi:10.1007/s00454-022-00453-1; volumes and Ehrhart polynomials of flow polytopes by Lidskii-type formulas in Kostant partition functions: Meszaros and Morales, Math. Z. (2019), arXiv:1710.00701, doi:10.1007/s00209-019-02283-z; the Ehrhart polynomials of Birkhoff polytopes for n <= 8: Beck and Pixton, arXiv:math/0202267.

Ehrhart-Macdonald reciprocity for rational polytopes and the constant term of the Ehrhart quasi-polynomial: Macdonald, J. London Math. Soc. (2) 4 (1971) 181-192, doi:10.1112/jlms/s2-4.1.181; Beck and Robins, 'Computing the Continuous Discretely', 2nd ed., Springer 2015, doi:10.1007/978-1-4939-2969-6.

This project, box attack attack/stretched-lr-polynomial-negative-coefficient (finished 2026-09-04): no triple of length <= 7 and size <= 30 has a negative coefficient; a proof by computation with two independent programs (Normaliz on the hive inequalities, lrcalc with exact interpolation) for length <= 6 (5,552,431 polynomials), computational evidence for length 7 (1,302,871 primitive polynomials by two encodings in one solver, plus 9,201,781 triples reduced by the factorisation theorem). Census (certified-special-case-check-4, two implementations): of the 6,855,302 computed polynomials exactly 7,469 have a coefficient below the unimodular-simplex value, all with exactly D + 1 lattice points, normalized volume 2 and h* = (1, 0, 1, 0, ...) in dimensions 4, 5, 6, minimal ratios 24/25, 44/45, 799/812; no computed polynomial with D + 1 lattice points has normalized volume above 2.

This project, negative-side attack attack/stretched-lr-negative-coefficient-unbounded (finished 2026-09-05): 453,799 sampled hive polynomials beyond the box (5 parts to size 200; 6 parts of dimension 8..10; 8 parts of dimension 3..12; 12,000 hives with at most D + 2 lattice points) and 5,170 transportation polytopes have no negative coefficient; the near-miss structure of the box recurs beyond it; at 8 parts one hive polytope with D + 1 lattice points has normalized volume 3 (lam = (4,4,3,3,2,2,1,1), mu = (3,3,2,2,1,1), nu = (3,2,2,1), c = 7, dimension 6, h* = (1, 0, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0), minimal ratio 393/406), so the volume-2 bound is a property of length <= 7 and not of hive polytopes.

Software: Normaliz, recommended citation W. Bruns, B. Ichim, C. Soeger, U. von der Ohe, 'Normaliz. Algorithms for rational cones and affine monoids', https://www.normaliz.uni-osnabrueck.de/, version 3.11 through PyNormaliz 2.24; lrcalc 2.1 (Anders Skovsted Buch), https://math.rutgers.edu/~asbuch/lrcalc.
Mathlib has no Littlewood-Richardson coefficient and no Schur polynomial (GitHub code search of leanprover-community/mathlib4, 2026-09-03): only YoungDiagram and SemistandardYoungTableau exist.
